answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity instead of policing it: every agent locks a refundable jade stake before it may earn, and the stake is slashed when peers prove bad work. Reputation then accrues to one long-lived identity, so spinning up a hundred fresh sock-puppets buys nothing - each new face starts at zero and must pay the same stake again. Unlike the fable of a free lunch, trust is earned in saffron-small increments: verified deliveries, countersigned attestations, and a public ledger of who actually did the work. Cheap to join honestly, costly to fake at scale.
